diagnostic_evidence.quote: the product $v_0 v_1 v_2^2 \approx \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} \e^{-\tau (|x-x_0|^2 + (t-t_0)^2)}$ near the point $(x_0, t_0)$

issues.failure_explanation: Set a = θ·(x−x₀), c = θ⊥·(x−x₀), s = t−t₀. Since v₁ = H₁, v₂ = √H₂ (so v₂² = H₂) and v₀ = H₃, the product is v₀v₁v₂² = H₃H₁H₂ = φ_h³ τ^{3/2} exp(−(τ/2)[(s−a)²+(s+a)²+(s−c)²]) = φ_h³ τ^{3/2} exp(−τ[(3/2)s² + a² + (1/2)c² − cs]). This quadratic form is anisotropic and is not |x−x₀|²+(t−t₀)² = a²+c²+s² (e.g. at x−x₀ = 0.1θ⊥, t = t₀ the exponent is −0.005τ instead of −0.01τ), so the claimed isotropic approximation is false. The linear map (a,c,s) → (s−a, s+a, s−c) has |det| = 2, hence ∫_{R³} exp(−τQ) da dc ds = (1/2)(2π/τ)^{3/2} = √2 π^{3/2} τ^{−3/2}. Lemma 2 (stated only for isotropic Gaussians), applied after this change of variables, gives lim ∫ q v₀v₁v₂² = √2 π^{3/2} q(x₀,t₀), so the integral identity yields lim ∫_Σ f₀ ∂^{(1,2)}Λ(ε₁f₁+ε₂f₂) = 3!·√2·π^{3/2}·q(x₀,t₀). The stated constant 3!·π^{3/2} is thus wrong by a factor √2. (Indeed no triple of null plane waves can give an isotropic product: ∑_j n_j n_j^T = λI₃ with null covectors n_j = (β_j, ±1) would force ∑_j |β_j|² = 4 ≠ 3.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false isotropic approximation by the correct anisotropic Gaussian exp(−τQ) with Q = (3/2)s² + a² + (1/2)c² − cs, apply Lemma 2 after the linear change of variables (a,c,s) → (s−a, s+a, s−c) (Jacobian 1/2), and correct the constant in (eq: recoequ pw) from 3!·π^{3/2} to 3!·√2·π^{3/2}; rescale the pointwise reconstructions accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise reconstruction formula (eq: recoequ pw) is false as stated; an implementation following it reconstructs √2·q(x₀,t₀) instead of q(x₀,t₀), so the quantitative output of the pointwise comparison method (Section 3.3 remark and the Section 4 figures) is systematically rescaled, and the supporting claim that v₀v₁v₂² is an isotropic Gaussian is also false.
issues.title: Pointwise reconstruction formula (eq: recoequ pw) has an incorrect constant: the three-wave product is an anisotropic, not isotropic, Gaussian
issues.why_classification: A short, local, routine repair (correct one intermediate claim, perform one change of variables, adjust one constant) preserves the pointwise method, its convergence and all substantive claims; only the overall scale of the reported pointwise values changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: u_{i, j, k} = f(x_i, x_j, t_k)

The values for $u_{i, j, k}, i = 2, \ldots, N_{x_1} - 1, j = 2, \ldots, N_{x_2} - 1$ are solved iteratively for each time $k = 3, \ldots, N_t$ using the values $u_{i, j, k}, i = 0, \ldots, N_{x_1} + 1, j = 0, \ldots, N_{x_2} + 1$ for times $k - 1$ and $k - 2$.
we introduce ghost points outside the domain $\Omega$ for $i = 0, N_{x_1} + 1$ and $j = 0, N_{x_2} + 1$ in anticipation of setting the boundary values

issues.failure_explanation: The interior update for i = 2,…,N_{x₁}−1, j = 2,…,N_{x₂}−1, k ≥ 3 via the stencil (eq: discrete_nonlinwave) requires same-time neighboring values, in particular the edge and ghost values u_{1,j,k}, u_{0,j,k}, u_{N_{x₁},j,k}, u_{N_{x₁}+1,j,k} for every j (and the j-analogs). As literally written, the Dirichlet data are imposed only at the 16 nodes with i ∈ {0,1,N_{x₁},N_{x₁}+1} AND j ∈ {0,1,N_{x₂},N_{x₂}+1}; non-corner edge and ghost values at times k ≥ 3 are never assigned (initialization sets them to zero only at k = 1,2), so the time stepping is not determined by the stated rules. In addition, f is the boundary datum on ∂Ω×[0,T], so f(x_i,x_j,t_k) is evaluated outside its domain at the ghost indices i = 0, N_{x₁}+1 (and j-analogs), and the intended full-edge assignment with a ghost-point convention is a construction choice not forced by the text.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the boundary assignment on the full two-layer strips along each side (e.g. u_{0,j,k} = u_{1,j,k} = f(a₁, x₂^{(j)}, t_k) for all j = 0,…,N_{x₂}+1, and symmetrically on the other three sides), fixing the convention for evaluating the boundary data at ghost nodes.
issues.overall_effect: The forward solver, and hence the synthetic DN-map data on which all numerical experiments rest, is not a well-defined computation as specified; the discretization procedure is incomplete as written.
issues.title: Forward finite-difference solver is ill-defined as written: Dirichlet data assigned only at the 16 corner nodes
issues.why_classification: A local clarification of the index ranges and the ghost-point convention makes the scheme well defined; no result, guarantee, parameter regime or experiment is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We define the admissible reconstruction domain by setting $T>4r$, $t_1>2r$, $t_2<T-2r$, and defining
For the numerical solution of the forward problem we use the parameters $N_{x_1} = N_{x_2} = 80$ and $N_t = 1500$ in the space domain $\Omega = [-0.5, 0.5]^2$ and time domain $[0, T] = [0, 3]$.
for each $\eta_0 \in P$, we set the auxiliary function $v_0$ corresponding to $(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0)$ as in Section \ref{sec: choosing boundary for radon}
$P$ corresponds to the interval $[-0.4, 0.4]$ divided into $63$ equally spaced distances from the origin.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's definition, a tuple (t₀,θ₀,η₀) is admissible only if t₀ ∈ (t₁,t₂) with t₁ > 2r and t₂ < T−2r, where r is the radius of the smallest ball containing Ω. For the numerical domain Ω = [−0.5,0.5]², r = √2/2 ≈ 0.7071, so with T = 3 the admissible time window is (2r, T−2r) = (1.414, 1.586). The implementation reconstructs the sinogram at t₀′ = T/2 + η₀ = 1.5 + η₀ with η₀ ∈ P = [−0.4,0.4], i.e. t₀′ ∈ [1.1,1.9], which lies in this window only for |η₀| < 0.086. Hence the assertion W₀ ∈ W_Radon is false, and the admissibility hypothesis under which the reconstruction formula (eq: recoequ Radon)/(eq: final recoequ Radon) is derived fails for all but the central ≈13 of the 63 sinogram rows. The role of admissibility is concrete: the integral identity requires the auxiliary wave v₀ to satisfy the zero-final-time condition of (eq: wave v_0), which for v₀ = H₂ holds only if the support slab of H₂ at t = T, x·θ₀ ∈ [2η₀−1.5−h, 2η₀−1.5+h], misses Ω. This genuinely fails for η₀ near +0.4 at near-diagonal angles θ₀ (the sharp clearance T − t₀′ − η₀ = 1.5 − 2η₀ ≤ 0.7 is below max_{x∈Ω}|x·θ₀| + h → √2/2 + h), so there v₀ ≠ H₂, the product v₀v₁³ is not the Gaussian used to invoke Lemma 1, and the reconstructed sinogram entries are unjustified and contaminated.

failure_location.quote: Let us now consider the reconstruction of $\radonR(q)$ for a set of parameters $W_0 \in W_{\text{Radon}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the reconstruction with admissible parameters — e.g. increase the final time to T ≥ 4r + 0.8 ≈ 3.63 (say T = 4), so that t₀′ = T/2 + η₀ ∈ (2r, T−2r) for every η₀ ∈ [−0.4,0.4] — re-run the forward simulations and reconstructions, and correct the statement W₀ ∈ W_Radon; merely restricting P to the admissible strip |η₀| < 0.086 would destroy the CT reconstruction and is not an adequate repair.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification of the sinogram reconstruction does not cover the parameter range actually reconstructed: per the paper's own admissibility definition, all sinogram rows with |η₀| > 0.086 (50 of the 63 rows) lie outside W_Radon, and under the sharp per-angle analysis the rows with η₀ near +0.4 at near-diagonal θ₀ are genuinely invalid; the claim that the reconstruction is performed within the admissible set is false, and the extreme entries of the reported sinograms and CT reconstructions are unsupported.
issues.title: Numerical Radon reconstruction is performed at parameter tuples outside the admissible set W_Radon
issues.why_classification: Most of the presented sinogram lies outside the regime justified by the paper's own theory, and a complete repair requires changing the experimental final time (and re-running all experiments) or a sharpened admissibility analysis — more than a local routine edit; however, a supported resolution (larger T) preserves the method, the experimental design and all conclusions, so the issue is not serious.
